head.meta_description: Pan-Asian catering in Dubai from AED 700pp — sushi and sashimi and more, with vetted chefs and full service. Bespoke menus for any event. Get a quote.
head.h1: Asian Catering in Dubai — Menus, Prices and What's Included

opening_paragraph: Asian catering in Dubai from myCHEF is priced from AED 90 per person delivered, or AED 700 with a chef cooking on site. The menu covers sushi, dim sum, Thai curries and wok live stations. A vetted chef cooks it on site, designs your menu with you, serves your guests and clears everything away.

Whether you want a sushi counter at a marina villa, a live noodle station at a corporate launch, or a full pan-Asian banquet for a wedding, myCHEF brings you the right specialist and runs the evening end to end. Send your date, guest count and venue, and you will have an itemised proposal promptly during our published business hours.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What does Asian catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Asian catering includes menu design and tasting, a vetted private Asian chef cooking on site, front-of-house service staff where needed, plating, and full setup and cleanup. One team runs the event from arrival to the last cleared plate. "Asian" here is pan-Asian: Japanese, Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, Korean and South-East Asian dishes drawn together into one coherent menu. Our asian catering services in Dubai cover every format, from a private dinner for six to a large event buffet. Because it is chef-led, not a reheated tray of asian food, catering quality holds from the first canapé to the final dessert. Everything is prepared fresh to your brief, with dietary needs, spice levels and presentation agreed in advance so nothing is left to guesswork on the day.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: A Taste of Our Asian Catering
replace_in_block.new_heading: Why choose myCHEF for Asian catering
new_paragraphs: MyCHEF was founded by a chef trained in some of Europe's most demanding kitchens, on one idea: you own the evening, we carry the work. MyCHEF is implementing a structured partner verification standard across its chef network, covering identity, trade licensing and permitted activities, food-safety and food-handler records, and references ; some stages are in place and the rest are being rolled out as part of a continuing review. We are honest about it, too: no system removes every risk, so we match each event to the chef well suited to it, which is what makes us a dependable Asian catering choice in the city.

For a refined Asian brief, that might be Ahmed Al-Rashid , who brings 18+ years across Dubai, London and Paris and applies classical fine-dining technique to pan-Asian menus, with every course timed, seasoned and plated to exacting standards, built in collaboration with the host. We have run asian catering alongside villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas across Dubai. Client reviews are published only as events are delivered.

Your Asian menu in Dubai is built around signature dishes and tailored to your guests. Popular choices include sushi and sashimi, dim sum and steamed bao, Thai green and red curries, pad thai and wok noodles, Korean fried chicken, satay skewers, bao sliders, and dessert options such as mochi and mango sticky rice. Every menu is bespoke: choose a single-cuisine focus (all-Japanese, all-Thai) or a true pan-Asian spread. Dietary versions are no trouble: vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free and nut-free dishes sit naturally within Asian cooking, and halal Asian menus are available on request. The chef balances familiar crowd-pleasers with a few refined plates so the menu feels considered, not generic. Portion counts, spice levels and plating style are all agreed at the tasting stage, so what you approve is exactly what your guests are served.

We provide Asian catering across every part of Dubai, bringing the chef and full setup to your address. That includes Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Marina, JBR, Downtown, Business Bay, DIFC, Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches, Jumeirah and the wider city, plus yachts, beaches and desert venues. Wherever you are, the same standard applies: a vetted chef, fresh cooking on site, and a clean handover. Explore related menus — Sushi and Healthy — or see all cuisines and sample menus . Planning a full event? Start at catering in Dubai .

add_block.new_heading: Asian catering for weddings, corporate events and parties
new_paragraphs: Asian catering suits weddings, corporate events and parties equally well because the food is interactive, colourful and scales cleanly. For weddings and engagements, a pan-Asian banquet or sushi and dumpling stations give guests something memorable to gather around. Corporate Asian catering in Dubai works for office lunches, product launches and gala dinners, where a live wok or ramen station doubles as entertainment and a talking point. For an asian party catering brief such as birthdays, pool days or house celebrations, grazing platters, bao buns and skewers keep the mood relaxed. We handle asian catering for events of every size, matching staffing and menu depth to your guest count. Tell us the occasion and we shape the format, whether that is elegant plated courses, a flowing buffet, or hands-on live stations that let guests watch each dish come together.

add_block.new_heading: The Asian catering menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: Below is the working list the specialist chefs we work with build from. Chinese, Thai, Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese are kept as named sections, not blended into one "Asian" bucket, because a panang curry and a miso nasu shigiyaki are not interchangeable and a buyer can tell. A typical Dubai buffet takes three to five cold starters, one soup, three or four hot appetisers, two or three noodle and rice dishes, two to four mains drawn across the national sections, and two desserts; live stations are chosen on top of that. Small party catering in Dubai runs from 10 guests, and a buffet line needs 20. Dishes are written out the way a restaurant menu writes them, with the composition stated, so you approve the plate, not the category. That specificity is the honest test of the best Asian catering in Dubai: a caterer who writes "Thai curry" has not decided which curry yet.
Cold starters and Asian salads
The opening spread, served cold and plated or set out before anything hot arrives. Choose three to five.
Thai papaya salad, pounded to order with chilli, lime and palm sugar
Thai larb gai — spicy minced chicken salad with toasted rice powder, mint and lime
Raw Thai citrus crunch salad with clementine
Thai noodle and Asian vegetable salad
Japanese goma salad in a toasted sesame dressing
Togarashi miso green bean salad
Sichuan bang bang protein salad
Asian slaw; bean sprout and cucumber salad
Beetroot and seaweed salad
Quinoa and edamame salad
Five-spiced salad with mushroom and carrot
Three-pepper Vietnamese salad with dehydrated nori and couscous
Teriyaki-glazed salad with asparagus
Asian protein and mango salad; pineapple, bamboo shoot and pepper salad
Black somen noodle salad, spicy peanut sauce, panko chicken
Rare teriyaki beef, udon noodles, pickled Japanese vegetables, fried onion, bonito dressing
Beef sirloin, pickled papaya, Asian greens, aromatic herb salad, nahm jim dressing
Soups
One or two on a buffet, or a single soup course on a plated menu. The thicker Thai and Chinese soups hold well in a station pot; the clear broths do not, so those are served from the pass.
Tom yum, and tom kha kai with coconut and galangal
Hot and sour soup; Manchow soup
Laksa soup; miso tofu soup
Lemon, coriander and glass-noodle broth
Mushroom, ginger and spinach broth
Sweetcorn clear soup; crab-stick soup
Dim sum and steamed bites

Better sold as its own bamboo-steamer station than as a chafing dish, because dim sum sits badly on a buffet line for more than a few minutes. Note the Dubai adaptation: shui mai is folded with chicken and char siu bao is made with barbecue chicken, so the section is halal by design, not by quiet omission.
Har gau — prawn dumpling in a translucent wrapper
Chicken shui mai
Char siu bao — barbecue chicken in a steamed bun
Chinese roast chicken bao bun
Gyoza, chicken or beef, steamed then crisped on one side
Steamed dumplings, and a vegetarian dim sum platter
Spring rolls served alongside as a combined dim sum and bao section
Hot appetisers, fried and skewered
Four to eight of these, and the same items double as the canapé tier for a standing reception.
Spring rolls — vegetable, cheese or chicken; butter chicken spring rolls
Chicken Manchurian bites; vegetable Manchurian balls
Chicken Shanghai; Shanghai fish bites
Schezwan chicken popcorn; sesame chicken fingers
Cottage cheese kung pao; hoisin barbecue chicken
Chicken teriyaki and yakitori
Chicken karaage — ginger, sesame, sweet miso
Tempura — vegetable, shrimp or lobster
Bang bang calamari; calamari tossed with sesame and soy
Dynamite shrimp; sambal terasi prawns; sesame fired prawns
Tofu dynamite; truffle edamame
Kushiyaki skewers — beef, lamb or mushroom
Chicken satay with peanut sauce — read the dietary note below before putting this on a mixed-group menu
Sushi, sashimi and the raw bar

A sushi set runs eight to ten roll types plus two to four nigiri and sashimi items. Rolled ahead for a boxed platter, or cut to order at a manned counter — the counter is a different product and is quoted as a station. The raw bar is also the one setup that goes anywhere in Dubai without a permission question: villa dining room, apartment, terrace, open public beach or yacht deck all take it, because there is no flame, no fuel and no extraction to approve. What it does need is cold chain. The fish is cut in the licensed kitchen, moved temperature-controlled and held on ice under shade, and outdoors between May and September that holding window, not the venue, is what decides how long the counter can run.
California roll and super California; spicy tuna; spicy salmon
Alaska roll; rainbow roll; dragon roll; Neptune roll
Kappa maki; sweet potato roll; crunchy crazy roll
Samurai roll; rock 'n' roll; sushi sandwich
Musashimaru sake, the Musa salmon roll
Forbidden roll, made on black sushi rice
Beef tataki roll; tempura prawn roll; salmon avocado roll
Uramaki — tuna, scallop, wagyu or duck
Nigiri — sake, tuna, kingfish, seabass, prawn
Take sashimi — tuna, whitefish, salmon, squid, steamed octopus, crabstick
Salmon sashimi; seabass ceviche
Noodles and rice

At least one noodle and one rice on every buffet. Noodles are the usual failure point of this cuisine on a buffet, so they are cooked in batches against the service timeline instead of being held from the start.
Pad thai; pad see ew; Thai drunken noodles with shrimp; kimchi phad thai
Hakka noodles; Hong Kong noodles; Singaporean noodles, and a vegan Singaporean version
Soy ginger flat noodles; chopsuey
Pancit canton; pancit bihon with chicken, lamb or shrimp
Jasmine rice; fried rice; coconut rice
Salt and pepper tofu bokkeumbap
Japanese donburi bowl; Korean vegan bibimbap
Chinese mains
Two to four selected. Each line carries its protein variants, so the vegetarian version sits on the same line as everything else, not in a separate afterthought section.
Sweet and sour — lamb, beef, chicken, fish or vegetable
Kung pao — chicken or vegetable
Manchurian in the saucy style — chicken or vegetable
Schezwan — chicken, fish or vegetable
Hunan; chilli — beef, chicken or fish
Oyster sauce — beef, chicken, fish or vegetable
Mapo tofu
Stir-fried Chinese greens in garlic pepper
Stir-fried wild mushroom in black bean sauce
Char siu grilled chicken; Peking-style duck served with pancakes
Thai mains
Two or three selected, with the heat level agreed at the tasting instead of assumed.
Thai green curry; Thai red curry
Massaman curry; panang curry
Pad kra pao, the holy basil stir-fry
Poached fish in Thai lemon chilli
Stir-fried seafood with Thai red curry
Stir-fried potato with scallions
Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese mains
Katsu curry, and a vegetarian Japanese katsu curry
Miso-glazed steamed fish
Miso nasu shigiyaki — aubergine, sesame, sweet miso
Stir-fried bok choy, lotus root and edamame in yuzu ponzu
Yakitori; Japanese kushiyaki — beef, lamb, mushrooms
Japanese vegetable donburi bowl
Grilled sambal chicken
Vietnamese turmeric grilled fish
Korean bulgogi and bibimbap
Live stations

One to three stations is the usual choice. A station only earns its cost when there is real theatre in it, so each of these is made in front of guests, not plated behind a screen. Stations depend on venue power, gas and ventilation clearance, and on the assigned culinary partner confirming both the equipment and the specialist chef for your date — that is checked before a station goes into your proposal.
Sushi and sashimi counter — maki, uramaki, nigiri and sashimi cut to order by a sushi chef
Dim sum steamer station, folded and steamed to order
Bao station; gyoza station
Wok station — Hakka noodles, fried rice, stir-fry and chow mein over high-output burners
Teppanyaki noodle bar on a flat-top grill
Hawaiian poke bowl bar, built to each guest's order from a chilled display
Vietnamese pho station; Tibetan thukpa station
Interactive hot pot — guests pick proteins, vegetables, noodles, sauces, rice and broth and cook at the table
Sides, sauces and condiments
The sauce list is written out, not left as "assorted sauces", because the sauce is where most of the dietary questions sit.
Stir-fry vegetables; tossed vegetables; edamame; steamed rice
Sweet chilli; Thai chilli; sesame soy; spicy mayo; coriander mint chutney
Desserts and drinks
Mango sticky rice; mochi
Matcha and coconut desserts; coconut sticky toffee
Coconut milk mango chia pudding, or the same served as a shooter
Fresh fruit cuts
Lemongrass iced tea; jasmine tea; black and green tea; tropical green fresh juice
Formats this menu is served in

The same list is built into a buffet, a plated multi-course menu, a canapé tier where maki, nigiri and sashimi sit on a spoon, glass or cucumber shell, bento boxes for boardroom lunches, or boxed sushi platters for drop-off. Presentation hardware — sushi boats and bridges, ceramic soy dishes, sharing plates and chopsticks — is quoted as a named add-on, so you can see whether it is in the number or not.
Halal and dietary notes on this menu

Every section above is built halal from the start: no pork anywhere, chicken shui mai and barbecue-chicken char siu bao in place of the versions most guests know, and a halal Japanese pantry using alcohol-free mirin and cooking sake. That substitution changes how a teriyaki reduces, which is why it is agreed with the chef in advance, not left to the day. Vegetarian and vegan guests are unusually well served by this cuisine — mapo tofu, Korean vegan bibimbap, kimchi phad thai, salt and pepper tofu bokkeumbap, Japanese vegetable donburi and vegetable katsu curry are all full dishes, not side plates. Two ingredients need naming out loud: satay and the spicy peanut sauces carry nuts, and soy sauce, tempura batter and most wheat noodles carry gluten.

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.
Running more than one cuisine across a multi-day celebration? Indian catering in Dubai and sushi catering are handled by the same team and quoted on one proposal.

add_block.new_heading: How is Asian catering served in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Asian catering is served three ways in Dubai: plated, buffet, or interactive live stations, and the format is chosen around your venue and event. Live stations are where Asian cuisine shines. A sushi counter, a wok station or a ramen bar becomes part of the entertainment, with the chef cooking to order in front of guests. Buffets and grazing tables work well for relaxed gatherings and larger numbers, while plated multi-course service suits formal dinners and weddings. For homes and villas we bring everything needed, working cleanly around your kitchen; asian home catering leaves your space exactly as we found it. On yachts, rooftops and desert setups we plan the logistics of power, prep space and timing in advance. Whichever format you choose, service, equipment and cleanup are included so you host without lifting a finger.

add_block.new_heading: How much does Asian catering in Dubai cost?
new_paragraphs: Asian catering in Dubai prices in two bands, and which one applies depends on whether you are buying the food or the chef. Delivered and buffet formats start from AED 90 per person for a working lunch, AED 120 for a standard event buffet, and AED 150 for a premium buffet or a live wok, ramen or sushi station. A chef cooking and serving on site — plated courses, or a counter worked in front of your guests all evening — is AED 700 to 950 per person, with a tasting menu and pairings from AED 1,400. Asian catering prices scale with the extras you choose, such as premium seafood, presentation hardware, or additional chefs and servers. Package options keep budgeting clear, and we quote every event as an itemised proposal so there are no surprises. Whether you want affordable Asian catering for a casual gathering or a luxury Asian catering experience for a landmark event, we build to your budget and tell you honestly what each tier delivers. For a full breakdown of what drives asian catering cost in Dubai, see our Dubai catering price guide or request an itemised quote for your date.
Asian catering price list

This is the published starting price for each format, so you can place your event before you enquire. The minimum order is AED 900, which is ten guests on the entry tier, and 5% VAT is added to the total.

add_block.new_heading: How to hire Asian catering in Dubai
new_paragraphs: To hire Asian catering in Dubai, share three things: your date, guest count and venue. We bring you a vetted chef whose strengths fit your brief, then send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day. You approve the menu (a tasting is available for larger events), we confirm dietary needs and timings, and on the day the chef and any service staff arrive with everything required. If you have searched "asian catering near me" and want a caterer who turns up on time, cooks fresh and cleans up, this is the process. As an established Asian catering company covering all of Dubai, we handle single dinners and recurring corporate bookings alike. There is no obligation in getting a quote. Tell us what you are planning and we will point you to the right option for your budget, honestly.

add_block.new_heading: Planning asian catering step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your proposal arrives.

Book as early as you can. As guidance, standard catering packages want about 72 hours, live cooking stations and multi-staff events 3–5 days, and weddings or complex corporate productions 7–14 days or more.
Confirm the menu for asian catering some 7 days ahead, once numbers stop moving.

Ask anyway if your date is sooner. We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. A asian at short notice is sometimes workable - availability is confirmed individually, never assumed.
Ask for dietary covers at the asian catering briefing stage instead of within 48 hours .
Check parking and lift access; your asian catering team is on site some 2 hours early.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.
